Subject: Post-call: SLOs we discussed + measurement runbook (next steps)

Hi Jackson — thanks again for a productive demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on scope for the SLO qualification run: 

What we heard you need:
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 120ms for inference at your median request length (~200 tokens) and <= 250ms for 1024-token tails.
- Concurrency/throughput: 400 concurrent active sessions for streaming endpoints, steady-state throughput ~3,200 requests/minute with 30% burst headroom.
- Streaming behavior: server-side partial frames, low tail jitter (p99 tail < 500ms), and deterministic token ordering for reranked outputs.

What Redwood will provide for the qualification run:
- A measurement runbook (attached) that defines precisely how we calculate p95/p99, warm/cold path definitions, and sampling rules for streaming tail latencies.
- An eval harness config (harness-config.yaml attached) and Docker image to run locally or in your lab for reproducibility.
- Recommended prompt set canonicalization rules and a seed list for reproducible sampling.

Action items I propose this week:
1) You share a representative prompt sample set and traffic mix (you mentioned an anonymized export) — we can accept a small JSON export or a Drive folder link.
2) We run an initial baseline on our staging fleet (non-production) and share the raw traces and calculations.
3) Joint run: we schedule a 2-hour measurement window (tentative: Oct 10) where we exercise streaming loads and capture KV-cache hit/miss metrics.

Attached: redwood_measurement_spec_v0.2.pdf (draft), harness-config.yaml (example).

If the scope above looks right, can you: (a) send the anonymized sample payloads, and (b) confirm whether procurement/legal want to be looped now or later?

Thanks —
Sofia

2) Traffic mix: 65% short prompts (~50 tokens), 25% medium (~250 tokens), 10% long/soak (~800-1024). We can export a 24-hour anonymized sample tomorrow (stripping user IDs).

Thanks — reviewed the sample payloads and the drive doc. High-level feasibility notes and a concise benchmark plan: 

Feasibility (quick):
- Staging hardware (A100 80GB equiv) should meet 150–250ms p95 for 256–1024 buckets with tuned batching and KV cache warm paths. Main risk is burst behavior and tail jitter under streaming if client interleaves many small frames.

Proposed measurement methodology (for reproducibility):
1) Canonical prompt sets: use the supplied quantify_prompt_samples_v1.json; we will canonicalize whitespace and normalize determiners per spec in the attached runbook to avoid tokenization-induced variance.
2) Sampling seeds: we will run 5 deterministic seeds per test (seeded RNG in the harness) and report mean and stdev. Each seed represents a 30-minute simulated workload slice.
3) Warm vs cold: define warm after 120s of steady-state for KV cache; cold starts will be measured separately and excluded from steady-state p95.
4) Streaming tail: measure per-session frame gap and p99 of frame-to-frame latency; capture tail jitter histogram and aggregate by request-length buckets.
5) Concurrency model: emulate 'session' concurrency (400 simultaneous open connections with independent token streams) rather than pure request concurrency; this better reflects their frontend usage.
6) Artifacts for reproducibility: Docker image id (redwood/harness:20281003-rc1), harness-config.yaml, raw trace exports (.parquet) and a short README with exact CLI commands.

What we need from Quantify before baseline run:
- Confirm traffic mix (short/medium/long percentage) and provide any special prompt normalization rules.
- A sanitized sample of KV cache keys (or representative key distribution) if they use per-customer cache keys.
- Approval to run the staging job on Oct 10 at 09:00 PT (2 hours).

If that all looks good I’ll spin up the harness, lock the quant profile to the recommended setting for long tokens, and post the Docker image + command line in the Drive link this afternoon.

—Dev
